1.title: Vosges Sandstone: A Light Terroir That Drains and Warms Quickly
1.html: Vosges sandstone (grès vosgien) is made of quartz sand grains cemented by a siliceous or iron-rich matrix, in places interlayered with clay. These soils are sandy, extremely well-drained and quick to warm — steep terrain makes full use of the heat released by the rock, creating an ideal microclimate.
2.title: The Sandstone Trio: Distinctive Vosges Sandstone Sites
2.items.0.label: Wiebelsberg (Andlau, 12.52 ha)
2.items.0.desc: Vosges sandstone overlain by Quaternary dissolution deposits, sandy, well-drained and quick to warm. Already listed in Stoltz's famous 1852 Grand Cru classification work. Authorised for Riesling, with a delicately floral style, noble backbone and excellent ageing potential.
2.items.1.label: Kessler (Guebwiller, 28.53 ha)
2.items.1.desc: Buntsandstein Vosges sandstone, with Muschelkalk limestone outcrops at the base. Documented as early as 1394 and sold commercially on its own from 1830. Mainly Gewurztraminer, intensely floral, complex and long-lasting but never coarse.
2.items.2.label: Kitterlé (Guebwiller, 25.79 ha)
2.items.2.desc: A steep slope with multiple aspects (south, southeast, southwest) and distinctive dry-stone terraces, a landform without equal in Alsace. Documented in 1699 and sold under its own brand from 1830. Riesling, Gewurztraminer and Pinot Gris are all excellent, with low yields bringing extreme concentration and ageing potential.
3.question: What historical feature do Kessler and Kitterlé, the two Guebwiller Grand Crus, share?
3.options.0: Both are the newest Grand Crus delimited in Alsace (2007)
3.options.1: Both were sold commercially under their own site names as early as 1830
3.options.3: Both are in the Bas-Rhin département
3.explanation: Kessler and Kitterlé are both in Guebwiller and share a long tradition of independent branding — as early as 1830 these two sites were already sold commercially under their own names, long before the 1975 Grand Cru classification, showing the lasting reputation these terroirs have enjoyed in Alsace's history.
4.keyPoints.0: Vosges sandstone: cemented quartz sand, well-drained and quick to warm, suited to steep terrain
4.keyPoints.1: Wiebelsberg (Andlau): listed in the 1852 classic classification, Riesling only, delicately floral
4.keyPoints.2: Kessler (Guebwiller): documented in 1394, mainly Gewurztraminer, independent brand since 1830
4.keyPoints.3: Kitterlé (Guebwiller): multi-aspect steep terraces, unique in Alsace, excellent with all three varieties
